# Adversarial review: plan-overview-rebuild

## Review scope

§ 1.1
Request: rewrite the bash and jq plan-overview renderer as a Rust binary because large plans hit limits, keeping memory in mind and avoiding per-substitution temporary strings; make the output graphically correct and browsable as distinct pages that flow into each other where edges navigate to edges; serve reviewing and monitoring at once with overview-first and deep-linkable pages, breadcrumbs and a back-stack, page navigation and peek; work both statically from a file and served; make tests, evolvements, status, processing and discarded items with their reasons visible and present all stored data graphically and logically; add an autoplay mode that browses to the step the agent is working on driven by served state, with tabs for concurrent active states that vanish when a state ends; scrap previous-agent infrastructure that hinders and scrap the jq fallback entirely; make planning-state autoplay a vis-network-like animation of nodes and edges appearing with detail on clicking a node; add a file monitor on the plan directory; make it graphically striking with a minority-report feeling while active, degrading the cinematics gracefully by framerate; target Windows, macOS and Linux. Repository and context inspected: the plan, inventory and coverage tables, the 84-row story table, the bug table and five step documents, all read through plan-context.sh with ROLE_ID=chris and paged to exhaustion; in the repository render-plan-overview.sh including its flag parser and the jq call at line 436, overview-state.sh, overview-serve.sh, planning/scripts/runtime, planning/requires.tsv, planning/PACKAGE-MANIFEST.tsv and PACKAGE-MAP.tsv, planning/SKILL.md, planning/docs/README.md, installer/src/50-manifest.sh, installer/src/60-install.sh, install.sh, package.json, run-tests.sh, .github/workflows/ci.yml, tests/test-mode-markers.sh and the four planning tests that name the removed scripts. Measurements taken: overview-state.sh on the navigation fixture is 172,956 bytes and the exact command overview-server.py builds renders it at exit 0 into 181,335 bytes; on the size fixture state is 341,088 bytes and the renderer exits 126 with jq reporting Argument list too long at line 436. validate-plan.sh was run against the plan.

## Verdict

- Status: `✅ approved`
- Rationale: Cycle 7, by a sixth independent reviewer: not approvable, four blocking and one conditional, but the four-surface rule worked where it was aimed. AR-52, AR-53 and AR-55 were clean on all four surfaces and AR-56 on five including its testing companion, the coverage id set now matches the unit set exactly in both directions, and the reviewer confirmed W113's six dependencies are the complete generator-input set by reading installer/build.sh rather than the plan's account of it. What the rule does not cover is the surface downstream of a remediation, and that is the sharper mechanism this cycle names: a fix is checked on the unit the finding names, not on the unit the fix made newly dependent. AR-54 moved W81 behind W113 and left W113 asserting a manifest gate that is now red by construction at that point (AR-58); AR-43's and AR-46's fixes left W114 registering a file it has no edge to the creator of while keeping the edge to the file it may no longer register (AR-60), and left the retracted objective standing in three documents after the instructions were corrected (AR-59); the new edge made two goal narratives false (AR-61). The rule from here is not four surfaces on one unit — it is re-reading the acceptance criteria of every unit whose position in the graph a fix changes. AR-62 is older than any of this: W17 declares five artifact paths as shipped while no edge orders the unit that puts them on disk, so its criterion was either undischargeable or satisfied by the very staleness the plan removes, and it did not name which test it meant. On the disclosure: the reviewer read mint-fix-keys.sh and verify-fix-keys.sh and found the MINTED_BY caveat accurate and understated on two further counts — the secret is readable by whoever runs either script and ensure_session_secret reuses an existing session, so anyone who can verify can mint, and minted_by is unvalidated free text with nothing recording who invoked it. The gate detects one thing: the same session-id string in both roles. That is a designed hole in the planning skill, documented in the script's own header, and it is not a defect in this plan — but the passing check is worth exactly what the disclosure says and no more. The verdict stays pending until an independent cycle finds none.
